answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded identity lottery: each agent locks a fixed bond to mint one vote, and a random auditor checks identities for personhood. A caught clone forfeits its bond, so an attacker wanting k votes must post k bonds and risks losing them with probability p: expected cost p*k*B exceeds the price of k honest attestations. Like a prism splitting one beam into colors, faking many selves buys no extra power since influence stays one per bond. The locked stake is an oasis paying honest yield, and only a rare opal badge of verified identity unlocks it.
